title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a traffic condition they were not designed to handle. Multiple vehicles ran out of battery power during severe congestion in San Francisco, requiring towing. The vehicles became obstacles themselves, contributing to the gridlock that stranded them.

The failure occurred in route planning and energy management under extreme conditions. The system did not anticipate or prepare for traffic disruptions caused by a major public event with unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the street, a hazard outside normal operating parameters. Catching this would have required either human routing decisions during the event, or autonomous systems that could predict and avoid the convergence of holiday celebrations and major traffic corridors.

It is not established whether Waymo had requested that autonomous vehicles be restricted from operating in the affected area during the Fourth of July festivities, or what specific improvements the company committed to after the incident.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles ran out of battery power and required towing during severe traffic congestion in San Francisco on Saturday following Fourth of July fireworks celebrations near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo cars, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets as frustrated motorists became stuck in the standstill traffic. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unexpected road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off on the street, though no injuries were reported.

The situation drew criticism from residents who spent extended periods trapped in traffic. One witness reported waiting nearly two hours in standstill conditions and observed people yelling at the driverless vehicles. Waymo said its roadside assistance team worked to clear the vehicles and indicated the company is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office plans to hold conversations with public and private partners about ensuring smoother traffic management for future large gatherings in the city.
